text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for tenant 'peregrine' on dedicated cluster prod-us-west-2 — reserved-capacity queue depth 95%, p90 latency 120s, errors rising. Incident ID INC-2031123. Link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC-2031123 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Alert triggered and routed to escalation policy 'dedicated-oncall' -> paging jordan (oncall).

jordan (oncall): ack — taking lead. looking at queue backlog and kv-cache behavior. will post commands I run.

maya (sre lead): @jordan good call. If kv-cache is hot we can try prefix eviction + enable burst capacity on the reserved pool. Also check model-serving pod OOMs (I saw a spike in the last 5m).

linh (infra): Uploading quick metrics snapshot: GPU util on r-peregrine-01 = 98%, host IO wait spiking. Several pods in Pending state due to node pressure. Logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/peregrine/INC-2031123

jordan (oncall): running scale and fallback routing now. patching reserved pool replica count to 6 -> 12 and enabling fallback route 'peregrine-fallback' for critical endpoints to reduce host-side load. Command I used:
```bash
kubectl -n inference scale sts r-peregrine-01 --replicas=12
apictl routing set-fallback --tenant peregrine --route critical --target peregrine-fallback
```

sam (eng ops): executed the scale command (confirmed by k8s events). New pods are starting, some pending due to image pull; I pre-pulled the image on hosts in us-west-2 to speed it up. :thumbsup:

opsbot: automated rollback disabled for INC-2031123 per jordan. Telemetry snapshotting enabled.

pagerduty: Incident INC-2031123 acknowledged by jordan (oncall). Further escalations paused.

maya (sre lead): Jordan — please run a targeted kv-prefix eviction for tenant 'peregrine' to clear hot segments. Example (redis):
```bash
redis-cli -h redis-01 -p 6379 --eval scripts/evict_by_prefix.lua peregrine:prefix
```
Also toggle reserved-pool burst queue: `poolctl set-burst r-peregrine-01 --capacity 30%`

jordan (oncall): ran eviction and bumped burst. Results: prefix hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 15%, p90 latency improved from 120s -> ~85ms on routing layer. Still seeing some 5xx coming from model-serving nodes; tracing: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/2031123456

linh (infra): model-serving node LR-14 had OOMs (kernel OOM killer) — restarted the node pool with larger host memory, bumped qps-slot for models serving Peregrine. Watching GC and allocation charts.

jordan (oncall): Customer impact summary for PD update: ~20% of Peregrine requests were routed to fallback read-only model for ~6 minutes during mitigation. Error rate peaked at 4.8% before mitigation, now down to 0.3%. No data exfiltration. Triage window: 30m.

maya (sre lead): Nice work. Jordan, please open an incident ticket and request a postmortem with root cause hypotheses (kv hot-prefix + pool sizing + image-pull delays). I'll join the postmortem.

jordan (oncall): creating INC-2031123 ticket and assigning postmortem to oncall and infra. Leaving handoff notes for next shift. :heavy_check_mark:

sam (eng ops): leaving a heads-up to Customer Success to prepare a brief notification if Peregrine asks. Contact: cs-peregrine@redwood.com

opsbot: Handoff reminder set — next oncall receives summary.

jordan (oncall): final note — keeping all mitigations active for 30m, will update PD and close alert when stable for 15m. Thanks everyone.
